newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Carpenter says Mt Kare assays confirmed.
newsitem.headline: Carpenter says Mt Kare assays confirmed.

text.p: Carpenter Pacific Resources NL on Thursday said a consulting geologists report showed enormous gold assays of more than 6,500 grams a tonne (g/t) from the Mt Kare project in Papua New Guinea could be independently validated.

It said the release of the original assay results on April 18 had led to numerous phone calls which queried whether the "bonanza grades in hole MK97-05 were caused by the drill just hitting a nugget of gold".
"This is not the case. The drill clearly intersected a rich vein of gold mineralisation in association with quartz-roscoelite alteration," Carpenter said.

It said consulting geologists Richard Newport and Associates had conducted more detailed analysis of the hole, including repeat assays to ensure that the results were a correct reflection of the mineralisation.

The report showed that a repeat assay from the interval 49.5 to 51.0 metres contained 6,549.0 g/t gold and 1,900.0 g/t silver and the entire interval of 31.8 metres from 27.0 metres to the bottom of the hole at 58.8 metres returned an average assay of 308.4 g/t of gold and 129.0 g/t of silver.

Carpenter's Matu Mining unit holds the exploration licence at Mt Kare while its joint venture partner Madison Enterprises Corp is entitled to 65 percent of the Mt Kare project once it has spent A$10 million.
Madison said last month that more than one million ounces of alluvial and colluvial gold were recovered from the Main Zone at Mt Kare between 1988 and 1990.
This was during a rush involving thousands of PNG nationals that ultimately drove away CRA Ltd from developing the hardrock at the site.
A majority-owned subsidiary of Ramsgate Resources NL owns one-third of Carpenter.
